question_text: An LGU allocated its P10,000,000 budget: Infrastructure 40%, Education 25%, Health 20%, Agriculture 15%. How much more is allocated to Infrastructure than Health?

hint_ladder.title: Focus on What the Question Is Really Asking
hint_ladder.text: The question isn't asking for the individual amounts of Infrastructure or Health. It's asking for the difference between them. So first, find the gap in percentages.

hint_ladder.title: The Simple Subtraction Rule
hint_ladder.text: When you see 'how much more' between two percentages of the same total, just subtract the smaller percentage from the larger one. Here, that's 40% minus 20%.

hint_ladder.title: Turn That Percentage Gap Into Pesos
hint_ladder.text: Now take that percentage difference (20%) and multiply it by the total budget. So 20% of P10,000,000 is your answer. Remember, 'percent' means 'per hundred' so 20% is 0.20.

hint_ladder.title: Almost There — Check Your Math
hint_ladder.text: 20% of P10,000,000 equals P2,000,000. That's the exact difference. Now look at the options — which one matches? You've got this.

A.text: This one is P1,000,000, which is only 10% of the budget. A smart student might get here by accidentally subtracting 30% from 40% (maybe mixing up Health's 20% with something else) or by misreading the percentages. It's an easy slip under time pressure.

B.text: P1,500,000 equals 15% of the budget. This is a classic case of grabbing the wrong number — Agriculture's 15% share. It's tempting to use a number that's already there, but remember, the question asks for the difference between Infrastructure and Health, not any single category.

C.text: Exactly right. The difference in percentage is 20% (40% minus 20%), and 20% of P10,000,000 is P2,000,000. Clean and simple.

D.text: P2,500,000 is 25% of the budget, which matches Education's share. It's very common to accidentally pick a number from the list of percentages given, especially Education since it's the second one mentioned. But the question is about the gap between two specific categories, not any single one.

next_time_rule: When a question asks 'how much more' between two percentages of the same total, always subtract the percentages first, then multiply by the total. Never grab a single percentage from the list — the difference is what matters.
deconstruct_text: Let's walk through this together. The total budget is P10,000,000. Infrastructure gets 40%, Health gets 20%. The question is: how much more does Infrastructure get? That's a difference question. First, find the gap in percentages: 40% minus 20% equals 20%. Now, turn that 20% into actual pesos. Remember, 'percent' means 'out of a hundred,' so 20% is the same as 0.20. Multiply: 0.20 times P10,000,000 equals P2,000,000. That's your answer. The mental trick here is to always ask yourself: 'Am I looking for a single amount, or the gap between two amounts?' If it's a gap, subtract the percentages first. It saves you from having to compute each individual amount and then subtract, which is slower and riskier under time pressure.
